youtube.baslik: How is agreement between studies in a meta-analysis measured? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: Heterogeneity means the results of the studies in a meta-analysis differ more than chance can explain. As a numerical measure, the I² statistic is given; it shows, as a percentage, how much of the variation comes from real differences. According to the Cochrane Handbook, an I² below 40 percent may often be unimportant, while above 75 percent is read as very high heterogeneity and calls a single pooled result into question; these limits are a rough guide.
